title: On the Square: the Locative Suffix -n

sections.content: Some place nouns use the superessive suffix -on/-en/-ön ('on/at') instead of -ban/-ben ('in') for their normal locative meaning. tér ('square') is one of them: with its front vowel, it takes -en, giving téren ('on/at the square').

items.english: The library is on the square.
The restaurant is on the square.

sections.content: There's no simple rule for which places use -ban/-ben versus -on/-en/-ön -- tér, utca and a few others take -on/-en/-ön by convention, so it's worth memorising 'a téren' and 'az utcán' as set phrases.
